title: Clothes
statementMd:
A little boy Gerald entered a clothes shop and found out something very unpleasant: not all clothes turns out to match. For example, Gerald noticed that he looks rather ridiculous in a smoking suit and a baseball cap.

Overall the shop sells $*n*$ clothing items, and exactly $*m*$ pairs of clothing items match. Each item has its price, represented by an integer number of rubles. Gerald wants to buy three clothing items so that they matched each other. Besides, he wants to spend as little money as possible. Find the least possible sum he can spend.

## Input

The first input file line contains integers $*n*$ and $*m*$ — the total number of clothing items in the shop and the total number of matching pairs of clothing items (![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/11d20cc08f8a72fe0056e3d0d36ad39fdff6b45f.png)).

Next line contains $*n*$ integers $*a*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{6}$) — the prices of the clothing items in rubles.

Next $*m*$ lines each contain a pair of space-separated integers $*u*_{*i*}$ and $*v*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *u*_{*i*}, *v*_{*i*} ≤ *n*, *u*_{*i*} ≠ *v*_{*i*}$). Each such pair of numbers means that the $*u*_{*i*}$-th and the $*v*_{*i*}$-th clothing items match each other. It is guaranteed that in each pair $*u*_{*i*}$ and $*v*_{*i*}$ are distinct and all the unordered pairs $(*u*_{*i*}, *v*_{*i*})$ are different.

## Output

Print the only number — the least possible sum in rubles that Gerald will have to pay in the shop. If the shop has no three clothing items that would match each other, print "-1" (without the quotes).

## Note

In the first test there only are three pieces of clothing and they all match each other. Thus, there is only one way — to buy the 3 pieces of clothing; in this case he spends 6 roubles.

The second test only has three pieces of clothing as well, yet Gerald can't buy them because the first piece of clothing does not match the third one. Thus, there are no three matching pieces of clothing. The answer is -1.

In the third example there are 4 pieces of clothing, but Gerald can't buy any 3 of them simultaneously. The answer is -1.
statementZhMd:
一个小男孩 Gerald 走进了一家服装店，却发现了一件非常令人不愉快的事情：并不是所有衣服都相互搭配。例如，Gerald 注意到自己穿着无尾礼服和棒球帽时显得相当滑稽。

这家商店总共出售 $*n*$ 件衣服，其中恰好有 $*m*$ 对衣服相互搭配。每件衣服都有一个价格，以卢布为整数表示。Gerald 想要购买三件彼此搭配的衣服。此外，他希望花费尽可能少的钱。请找出他可能花费的最小金额。

## 输入格式

输入文件的第一行包含整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$ ——商店中衣服的总数以及相互搭配的衣服对数 (![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/11d20cc08f8a72fe0056e3d0d36ad39fdff6b45f.png))。

下一行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*a*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{6}$）——每件衣服的价格，单位为卢布。

接下来的 $*m*$ 行中，每行包含一对由空格分隔的整数 $*u*_{*i*}$ 和 $*v*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *u*_{*i*}, *v*_{*i*} ≤ *n*, *u*_{*i*} ≠ *v*_{*i*}$）。每对数字表示第 $*u*_{*i*}$ 件衣服和第 $*v*_{*i*}$ 件衣服相互搭配。保证每对中的 $*u*_{*i*}$ 和 $*v*_{*i*}$ 不同，并且所有无序对 $(*u*_{*i*}, *v*_{*i*})$ 都不相同。

## 输出格式

输出一个数——Gerald 在商店中必须支付的最小金额，单位为卢布。如果商店中不存在三件彼此搭配的衣服，则输出 "-1"（不含引号）。

## 说明

在第一个测试中，只有三件衣服，并且它们彼此都相互搭配。因此，只有一种购买方式——买下这三件衣服；此时他需要花费 6 卢布。

第二个测试中同样只有三件衣服，但 Gerald 无法买下它们，因为第一件衣服与第三件衣服不搭配。因此，不存在三件彼此搭配的衣服。答案为 -1。

在第三个样例中有 4 件衣服，但 Gerald 无法同时购买其中的任意 3 件。答案为 -1。
